description_full: Reynolds Consumer Products Inc. produces and sells products in cooking, serving, cleanup, and storage, and tableware product categories in the United States and internationally. The company operates through four segments: Reynolds Cooking & Kitchen Essentials, Hefty Waste & Clean-Up, Hefty Home & Tableware, and Hefty Storage & Organization. The Reynolds Cooking & Kitchen Essentials produces branded and store brand aluminum foil, disposable aluminum pans, parchment paper, freezer paper, wax paper, butcher paper, plastic wrap, baking cups, oven bags and slow cooker liners; Branded products are sold under Reynolds Wrap, Reynolds KITCHENS and EZ Foil in the United States and selected international markets, under ALCAN in Canada, and under Diamond outside North America. The Hefty Waste & Clean-Up produces branded and store brand trash bags; Branded products are sold under Hefty Ultra Strong, Hefty Strong, Hefty Essentials, and Brute in the U.S. and select international markets. The Hefty Home & Tableware sells branded and store brand disposable and compostable plates, bowls, platters, containers, cups and cutlery. The Hefty Storage & Organization produces branded and store brand food storage bags; Branded products are sold under the Hefty brand in the U.S., and internationally as Reynolds, Diamond, or Hefty Basics depending on region. This segment also includes the specialty business providing Fresh-Lock and Slide-Rite resealable closure systems. Reynolds Consumer Products Inc. was founded in 1947 and is headquartered in Lake Forest, Illinois. Reynolds Consumer Products Inc. operates as a subsidiary of Packaging Finance Limited.

financial_summary: Reynolds Consumer Products Inc. is a mid-cap consumer cyclical business with a $5.1B market cap on $3.7B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -1% over the past three years — essentially flat, and a business treading water is rarely a path to compounding.

Returns on capital run at 10% against a 7% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, and 25% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $316M in free cash flow — roughly 8 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.58× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.3× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage runs at 5.6×.

Shareholder yield of 3.7% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 74% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 1.6× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
